plan_tool: init-block P needs G3 (the plan-A/B record derived from Gate B's verdict) as blocks A, certify, B and C do, and block B complete and sealed (G5, as certify and B need block A). Its jobs file is exactly {"launches": [{"deal": [0]}]}: a judge launch (addendum 40 point 7), a hosts or second-phase launch, a dealt pod twice or unknown, or a reused run refuses. Every P job is checked at init and again at release (plant_job_problem): kind arm, a plant arm, a pilot seed, no role, no points. The edit is bound at init too (bind_plant_edits: the dry run refuses without the sealed edit record) and again at release through resolve_edit (a missing record, two sources, a missing or changed file refuses). deal P prints the rule. P's funding record is its own; addendum 36's start-from-the-balance record is accepted as for any block.

The binding to REQ-8's record (an addition the lead keeps or drops; addendum 40 point 5 asks for a separate key-only binding check): record-sealed for a plant arm, and every binding at init and release, read REQ-8's record at its pin (stage1_rules.D2_REQ8_RECORD, already read by key for J5 and J8) and require full_files['edits/planted_k37.json'] (stage1_rules.PLANT_EDIT_FILES; the name scripts/stage1/build_plant.py write_location writes) to equal the recorded SHA-256. So only the plant build's own planted_k37 file can be recorded for a0_plant, and the lead never opens it: shasum prints its SHA-256, record-sealed refuses a wrong file. The refusal names the arm and the file name only.

The runner (setup/job_runner_stage1.py): after a complete plant-arm job it writes the readable job-I/arm-adapter-fingerprint.json once (exclusive create, canonical JSON): kind 'stage1 arm adapter fingerprint', version 1, job, arm (a0_plant), seed, steps, unit, COMPLETE.json SHA-256, checkpoints {e1 (states/e1/state.json's, equal to COMPLETE.json's), q}, identity {manifest_sha256, training_identity}; never the edit's name or any other edit field (unit_fingerprints, shared with K6's a0 record, reads those fields only). If it cannot be written the unit stands and the reason is recorded (K6's rule). seal.py's READABLE_PATTERNS (*adapter-fingerprint*.json) already class it readable, so seal.py is unchanged.

record-done HOST prints plant_units [{job, arm, seed, unit (path from the repository root), complete_sha256, fingerprint_record {path, sha256} | null}]: the pilot reader's inputs, read by key. A listed fingerprint record must be this run's (kind, version 1, job, arm, seed, int steps, unit, COMPLETE.json SHA-256, a 64-hex e1, q 64-hex or null, no edit field) or record-done refuses; a missing one prints null and plan.json keeps the runner's reason (fingerprint_record_problem). No judge runs for block P: it completes once its host is recorded done and seal.py block P seals it with no judge record and no judges/P/ (tested: 22 files, 15 sealed, 7 readable for the three units). A crashed run is re-run once from P's contingency (defer).

Money, Branch 128 (the kit's own numbers on a synthetic plan with the Gate A fixture's e1 upper and training seconds): one a0_plant arm job measured upper 4,144 s, start requirement 9,418.29 s; one pod with the three: cap 5.75 h (as the check report's 1.1 expects), guard $16.6375 -> $16.64, upper spend $7.4345 -> $7.43 (as expected), need base $16.64, 1.25 x = $20.80, contingency $4.16 (one re-run on a new pod $3.31, not two); worst case at the cap 5.75 x $1.79 = $10.29. Under Branch full: measured 4,637 s, cap 6.25 h, upper spend $8.17. The check report's $21.34 was READY's figure under another rounding; the kit's need is $20.80.

Blinding inside the kit (addendum 40 point 3; the check report's B1): the edit is named by SHA-256 everywhere (the sealed record, plan.json's job edit {path, sha256, source}, the pack's edits/<SHA-256>.edit.json, calibrate's --arms edit-<SHA-256>, the unit folder name); no kit command parses the edit file or a unit's COMPLETE.json beyond the fingerprint and identity fields. A test runs the whole planning and recording path on a synthetic kit with a synthetic edit whose name field (and every other text field) holds a sentinel, and REQ-8's record whose unit and leaf fields are sentinels, and asserts that no sentinel reaches stdout, stderr, plan.json, operator-actions.jsonl, hosts/, seals/, the finisher's finished.json, verified.jsonl and log records, JOB-DONE.json, a cost ledger or a fingerprint record, while the units' COMPLETE.json, edit.json, summary and state files (sealed class) do hold it. The runner test does the same on a synthetic pod (the fake engine writes the edit summary into COMPLETE.json and the run's edit.json copy).

The binding to REQ-8's record is an addition: record-sealed for a plant arm refuses unless REQ-8's record (pinned, read by key) lists the recorded SHA-256 for edits/planted_k37.json. It replaces no ruling (the separate key-only binding script of addendum 40 point 5 may still be built); if the lead drops it, the three refusals at record-sealed, init and release go with it (plant_edit_problem) and the tests that assert them.

The host prefix is p (hosts p-1, ...). A prefix holding 'plant' would put every kit record of the block (hosts/plant-1/finished.json, the launch and finisher logs named after the host) under the never-open path rule, which the lead must open to run the block; so the prefix is neutral and the never-open rule of addendum 40 point 3 (retrieved/ and every plant-arm unit folder) stays an explicit rule.
